note: _comedens cum eo et bibens familiariter_ (Vg, NVg) – eating with him and drinking familiarly. The Hebrew has: they ate and drank and he stayed there.

_ecce concubina eius iacebat ante ostium sparsis in limine manibus_ – behold, his concubine lay before the door with her hands spread on the threshold. **(1)** Why with her hands spread (_sparsis manibus_)? Because this wording echoes Vergil’s _Aeneid_ IV, 663–665, the suicide of Dido. – Neil Adkin: The Death of Dido and the Vulgate Text of the Gang-bang at Gibeah. _Maia_ 63 (2011) 451–454. – **(2)** Note the elegant hyperbaton: _sparsis in limine manibus_ (instead of _sparsis manibus in limine_). ▲
